capture_review.scope: Bounded source review plus edits only to existing CUDA TopK Graph tests; no build, GPU, native process or product implementation edits by reviewer.

original_gap.fact: Nonempty TopK was uniformly Managed and capture incompatible, including the new fixed two-kernel arg_tiles program. Thus ordinary RequirePrepared filtering and RequireCapture were both blocked.

current_root_fix_review.conclusion: No source-level blocker found for the narrow arg_tiles capability change. Root owns implementation and actual validation.
facts: Program is zero-initialized by describe; configure_typed is the sole writer of nonzero arg_tiles, only for TopK K=1, more than one row and width>2048. No model, vocabulary or batch-size whitelist is needed.

Cold configure resolves both kernel attributes and reserves the complete caller-owned aligned partial workspace. The successful arg_tiles submit branch only launches fixed geometry kernels and reports launch status; it does not call CUB host dispatch, shape search, heap allocation, packing, device-to-host validation or stream synchronization.

runtime(program) is shared by proposal and selected prepared artifact. Root now marks Gather or nonzero arg_tiles Prepared/capture-compatible, with caller workspace and concurrent Invocations; empty programs retain the existing no-op Prepared contract.
The same runtime fact now gates external-capture rejection and the old error-path host synchronization. Single-row TopK1, short multirow TopK1, K>1 and Scan remain Managed and uncapturable.

Each Invocation stores its own caller workspace pointer; Graph allocations and captured command arguments are per Invocation. Concurrent direct callers must still supply distinct writable workspace, as required by the existing borrowed-workspace contract.
The first tile kernel may be accepted before the second finish launch fails. The current CUDA helper returns only cudaError_t and cannot prove that an error means zero native work was accepted.

Provider retains accepted_command(status), conservatively retaining the original ordered prefix and Completion machinery. Do not turn a failed tiled submission into rejected solely from the helper return status.

Prepared arg_tiles no longer runs cudaStreamSynchronize on an error. Capture failure must terminate/abort the original recording, not synchronize a capturing stream; original CUDA abort_capture ends and destroys the recording.
This is a source-level error ownership review, not an injected first-success/second-failure runtime proof. No new failure hook was added.

failure_source_review.scope: Read-only narrow source review of prepared tiled TopK1 failure retirement and capture compatibility; no product changes, build, or GPU execution.

conclusion.assessment: No blocking defect found in the reviewed change. Prepared tiled TopK1 uses the existing accepted-prefix retirement and capture-abort paths; managed dispatch retains its previous synchronization behavior.

checks.claim: Proposal, preparation, and submit use the same configured-program classification.
checks.reason: runtime(program) is evaluated after collectives::configure. Nonzero arg_tiles is set only for tiled TopK1; Gather and count-zero retain their existing prepared behavior. submit derives managed from that same runtime() function.

checks.claim: The newly capturable TopK1 path has fixed kernels and caller-owned workspace, with cold code loading.
checks.reason: configure_arg_tiles checks/materializes both kernel functions and validates thread limits; configure reserves the per-row partial workspace. Hot tiled submit launches the two fixed kernels and checks each launch result, without CUB dispatch, allocation, or host arithmetic readback.

checks.claim: Failure after a possible accepted prefix does not release the original sequence or borrowed workspace early.
checks.reason: After attempting the native leaf, provider returns accepted_command(status), even when the first or second launch reports an error. This conservatively fences even an empty failed launch. QueueSequence ORs acceptance and preserves its first error. CUDA finish records an event, or uses original-stream fallback if recording fails. poll remains pending until actual retirement evidence; the diagnostic hint itself is not that evidence.

checks.claim: Normal operation and Graph owners remain attached to asynchronous completion.
checks.reason: Direct Operation submission attaches Invocation lifetime after accepted finish. Graph enqueue records EnqueueResult before stopping on its error. Cold Graph capture finish attaches preparation retention before waiting, so errors or abandonment do not rearm/release the borrowed Invocation/workspace solely because the provider returned an error.

checks.claim: Capture errors are terminated before sequence retirement and cannot publish an artifact as prepared.
checks.reason: A recorded-step failure causes abort before sequence finish; backend abort ends capture and destroys any returned graph. A capture-end/instantiate error cleans its state and clears recording before finish. Graph marks replay unprepared and returns the original failure; failed end cannot yield a usable capture artifact.

checks.claim: Managed dispatch semantics and zero-work behavior are preserved.
checks.reason: Non-tiled TopK/Scan remain managed and reject external capture; their existing synchronization on native-leaf error is retained. TopK count zero returns no_op before payload pointer access. Removing provider-side synchronize applies only to prepared kernels; backend exceptional fallback waits and Graph cold preparation waits are still allowed.

limits: Source review only: no injected second-launch failure, capture failure, event-record failure, or asynchronous device failure was executed by this reviewer.
No throughput or synchronization-cost claim; no review of unrelated collectives math or the full architecture.
Managed error synchronization still ignores its own result as before; this change does not alter that pre-existing behavior.
Batch-size changes can alter legal BF16 reductions. Greedy mismatches are reported, never filtered or promoted to quality acceptance.
These are two synchronized synthetic fixed-token sessions, not free-running serving latency or a four-user forecast.
Same C/N/R and tokens do not make backing allocations or failure/cancellation contracts identical. Hyle hasN+R snapshot pools; peer can update unretained native versions in place.
Memory processes are sampled separately; unknown/missing counters remain null. One desktop GPU, fresh processes, OS page cache not cleared.

ready_baseline.definition: Last process-running sample between received ready and earliest actual prefill-begin; null when none exists.

limits: All boundaries are parent receipt times from live stderr, not exact device/allocator times. Phase names are discovered from actual markers, including session prefixes.
Missing/duplicate/reversed boundaries have no derived phase values; short/full-hit phases may have zero samples. Null bytes remain null, never zero-filled.
PSAPI/PDH sampled maxima are lower bounds, not physical allocation totals. Dedicated/shared separate maxima must not be added; total uses simultaneous available counters.
Neighbor-sample phase deltas include bracket age and may include subsequent work or teardown; they do not attribute allocations or frees.
Old runs whose observer dropped session-prefixed markers cannot have timestamped phase samples reconstructed from untimestamped stderr. This adapter does not rewrite them.
Memory sampling is independent and never contributes to unmonitored timing denominators.

limits: Headline rates are process medians of per-process token-count/summed wall time; no averaging instantaneous or per-token TPS. Total is198/requestwall, startup-inclusive is a separate198/startupwall metric.

Current vs before decode and total min/max ranges overlap. Three fresh processes per arm, no exclusive GPU/fixed clocks/page-cache reset or statistical significance; the small difference is not evidence of a stable speedup.

Both arms still have1234 logical steps and the same native TopK1 kernels; prepared/capture eligibility can combine command recording differently. No new native profile was run here, so do not infer physical GraphLaunch counts or a specific component's time saving from capability flags.

Same fixed token inputs, same198 IDs and finite vectors do not establish cross-engine BF16 quality acceptance; this synthetic synchronized two-session teacher-forced workload does not establish free-running serving latency or four-user scaling.

Both preserve full KV+conv/GDN state, but Hyle immutable N+R version backing and peer in-place/native context contracts are not identical. Hyle state backing103710768 bytes vs peer105971712; memory sampler separately observes IO/weights/workspace/runtime.

Sampled per-PID PDH GPU and CPU working-set peaks are lower bounds, not exact allocation maxima; CPU private commit is not private resident memory. Simultaneous GPU-total peak is not the sum of dedicated/shared independent maxima.

Memory was sampled in separate processes at requested10ms; actual gap statistics are reported. Marker timestamps are reader receipts with brackets, not exact device boundaries; two sessions' overlapping phase windows must not be added. Missing ready-to-firstP samples mean ready-to-inference allocation delta is unknown.
After-window nvidia-smi utilization is a rolling snapshot immediately after inference and may include the just-finished consumer. It cannot alone identify external background GPU activity.
